_note: Situations grounded in the ODL PM, Learning Design and Media SOPs. Each has exactly one full-credit answer; other answers earn partial credit and explain why in 'why'. 'who' is the person shown; 'mood' their face when the situation appears; 'reaction' their face after the choice.

events.title: Tomorrow's Meeting Has No Agenda
events.text: {ld} stops by: "Tomorrow's content mapping meeting with {faculty} is our first real working session. Is there an agenda? I need {fobj} to bring {fpos} old syllabus and {fpos} top three outcomes."

choices.label: Draft the agenda with {ld} today, list what {faculty} should bring, and send it with the materials so {fsub} can prepare.
choices.outcome: {faculty} arrives with {fpos} syllabus and outcomes. The meeting ends early with decisions made.
choices.why: The SOP asks the PM to draft every agenda with the lead designer or producer and share materials ahead, especially for busy faculty.

choices.label: Write a quick agenda yourself and send it tomorrow morning.
choices.outcome: The agenda goes out, but {faculty} hasn't seen it before the meeting and arrives without {fpos} syllabus.
choices.why: Having an agenda helps, but it missed {ld}'s goals for the meeting and gave the faculty no time to prepare.

choices.label: Skip the agenda; it's a casual first meeting.
choices.outcome: The hour drifts. You leave with a second meeting to schedule.
choices.why: Meetings without an agenda wander, and faculty time is the scarcest resource on the project.

choices.label: Postpone the meeting a week so there's time to prepare.
choices.outcome: You get prepared, but lose a week of design time and {faculty} has to rearrange {fpos} calendar.
choices.why: A day is enough time to draft an agenda; moving the meeting costs schedule and goodwill.

debrief.concept: Meetings are the PM's main tool. Prepare them so faculty time isn't wasted.
debrief.independent: Agree the meeting goals with the lead designer, draft the agenda from the template, and send it with any materials a day or more ahead.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue. This is core PM work.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Managing Meetings, Meeting agendas

events.title: Can We Just Move the Date?
events.text: {ld} needs one more week on the course map. "Can you just slide it in Asana? It's only a week." The timeline was reviewed by the ODL directors last month.

choices.label: Map the knock-on effects with {ld} and {mp}, propose how to absorb them, then take the change to the directors for approval before updating Asana.
choices.outcome: The directors approve a one-week shift with scripting starting in parallel. Everyone sees the same dates.
choices.why: Once a timeline is established, changes need director review. Bringing the knock-on effects and a plan is exactly how to ask.

choices.label: Slide the date in Asana. It's only a week.
choices.outcome: Asana updates. {mp} finds out two weeks later that scripting now collides with another shoot.
choices.why: Quiet changes skip the approval the SOP requires and hide knock-on effects from the rest of the team.

choices.label: Hold the date. Ask {ld} to finish on time.
choices.outcome: {ld} delivers on time, but the assessment plan is thin.
choices.why: Holding a date by pressure alone moves the problem into quality.

choices.label: Keep the date by finishing the assessment plan later, during development.
choices.outcome: The course map lands on time; the assessment work shifts into development.
choices.why: A sensible trade-off, but it changes the plan without the team or directors agreeing to it.

choices.label: Tell {sup} that {ld} wants more time and ask what to do.
choices.outcome: {sup} asks what the change affects. You don't know yet.
choices.why: Escalating is right here, but bring the impact and a recommendation, not just the request.

debrief.concept: Change control: know who approves timeline changes, and surface knock-on effects before asking.
debrief.independent: Meet with the affected people, review the timeline, list knock-on effects and how to absorb them. Then get a clear approval and update Asana.
debrief.escalateWhen: Here escalation is required: established timelines change only with director approval. Come with the analysis.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Design phase; When Things Go Wrong, With Timelines

events.title: The Scripting Workshop Gets Heated
events.text: Forty minutes into the scripting workshop, {faculty} and {mp} are arguing about tone. {Fsub} wants formal lectures; {mp} is pitching the conversational style from the lookbook. Half the agenda is untouched.

choices.label: Restate the meeting goals, summarize both views, and park the tone question for a short follow-up where {mp} shows two sample clips.
choices.outcome: The room calms down. You finish the agenda, and the sample clips settle tone the next week.
choices.why: The SOP's first move: remind everyone of the objectives, summarize, and refocus. Parking the debate keeps the meeting productive.

choices.label: Professionally end the meeting and reschedule.
choices.outcome: Things cool off, but you lose the rest of the agenda and a week of scripting.
choices.why: Ending a meeting is a valid SOP option when it's unproductive, but try refocusing first.

choices.label: Side with {faculty}. It's {fpos} course.
choices.outcome: {faculty} is satisfied. {mp} goes quiet for the rest of the meeting.
choices.why: The PM facilitates; picking a side undermines the producer's expertise and skips the evidence.

choices.label: Let them work it out; creative tension is healthy.
choices.outcome: The meeting runs over and ends without decisions.
choices.why: Keeping meetings on task is the PM's job.

choices.label: After the meeting, ask {sup} to step in on the tone decision.
choices.outcome: {sup} suggests the sample-clip approach you could have proposed in the room.
choices.why: This is a facilitation problem you can handle. Escalate only if the disagreement persists.

debrief.concept: Facilitation: restate goals, summarize, refocus, and know when to end a meeting.
debrief.independent: Remind people what the meeting is for, summarize where things stand, and move the disagreement to a follow-up with evidence (sample clips, lookbook). End the meeting professionally if it keeps going sideways, and do an internal touchbase before the next one.
debrief.escalateWhen: Bring in ODL leadership when a disagreement keeps blocking decisions across meetings.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: When Things Go Wrong, In Meetings

events.title: Silent Faculty
events.text: {faculty} hasn't answered {ld}'s or {mp}'s last emails. Scripts are due in two weeks. {ld}: "I've sent three messages. {mp} sent two more."

choices.label: Route all requests through you, and propose a standing 15-minute Friday check-in plus comments in the script Google Docs.
choices.outcome: {faculty} accepts the Friday slot. Fewer emails, faster answers.
choices.why: For hard-to-reach faculty the SOP says streamline communication through as few people as possible, limit emails, and use short check-ins and async comments.

choices.label: Send one long email listing everything the team needs from {fobj}.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} replies to the first item and misses the rest.
choices.why: One channel is better, but a long list buries the asks.

choices.label: Ask {ld} and {mp} to each follow up again.
choices.outcome: {faculty} now has seven unread emails from ODL.
choices.why: More senders means more noise. This is the opposite of what the SOP recommends.

choices.label: Brief {sup} on the risk to the script deadline, what's been tried, and your proposed check-in plan.
choices.outcome: {sup} agrees with your plan and suggests you try it first.
choices.why: A solid escalation, but this is a communication fix within your control.

choices.label: Forward the thread to {sup}: "Faculty isn't responding."
choices.outcome: {sup} asks what you've tried and what you recommend.
choices.why: Escalating without options hands the thinking upward.

choices.label: Wait. {Fsub}'s probably just busy with midterms.
choices.outcome: Another week passes in silence.
choices.why: Waiting lets the risk grow.

debrief.concept: Stakeholder communication: fit the channel to the person.
debrief.independent: Find out how the faculty member prefers to communicate. Funnel requests through one person, keep emails few and short, and use brief standing check-ins and doc comments.
debrief.escalateWhen: Bring in ODL leadership when silence persists after you've changed the approach and the delivery date is at risk.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Challenging Faculty; Faculty Availability

events.title: {faculty} Is Drowning
events.text: {faculty} emails late at night: "Scripts, quiz questions and reading lists are all due the same week as my midterms. I can't do all of this."

choices.label: Re-pace with {ld} and {mp}: stagger the deadlines, and have {ld} draft quiz questions from the course map for {fobj} to edit.
choices.outcome: "This I can do." {Fpos} drafts start arriving again.
choices.why: The SOP asks the PM to watch faculty pacing, and to work offline on drafts the faculty can react to.

choices.label: Push all {fpos} deadlines back two weeks.
choices.outcome: {Fsub}'s relieved, but production and the build now start late.
choices.why: Moving everything ignores the knock-on effects on media and design, and skips approval.

choices.label: Remind {fobj} the charter set these dates.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} goes quiet.
choices.why: The charter matters, but this is a pacing problem the team can solve together.

choices.label: Ask {sup} for approval to re-sequence {fpos} deliverables, with a proposed staggered schedule.
choices.outcome: {sup} approves. The new schedule helps, a few days later than it could have.
choices.why: Fine if the re-pace changes milestone dates; otherwise you can rearrange within the window yourself.

debrief.concept: Pace the faculty: steady progress beats a pile-up.
debrief.independent: Stagger asks, let designers and producers draft so faculty only react, and keep the delivery date fixed while moving work within it.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if re-pacing moves established milestones; those need director approval.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Development phase note on pacing; Faculty Availability

events.title: The 5-Minute Video Is 14 Minutes
events.text: {mp} is reviewing scripts: "Module 3 reads at about 14 minutes. The charter says 5-minute videos. {Fsub}'s attached to every word."

choices.label: Remind {faculty} the charter commits to 5-minute videos and make trimming a priority, with {mp} marking which parts could move to a reading.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} trims to 6 minutes and moves the rest to a reading. {mp} can live with 6.
choices.why: This is the SOP's own example: point to the charter, prioritize the trim, and offer an in-scope alternative.

choices.label: Split it into two videos.
choices.outcome: Everyone's happy until post-production runs long.
choices.why: It adds a deliverable that isn't in the charter.

choices.label: Film it as written and cut it down in editing.
choices.outcome: The shoot runs long and the edit becomes a puzzle.
choices.why: Problems left in the script get more expensive in production and post.

choices.label: Ask {mp} to rewrite it shorter himself.
choices.outcome: {faculty} rejects the rewrite as "not my voice."
choices.why: Producers review scripts, but the content belongs to the faculty member.

choices.label: Ask {sup} to talk to {faculty} about the length.
choices.outcome: {sup} points back to the charter, just as you could have.
choices.why: Scope reminders are the PM's job first. Escalate if creep keeps coming back.

debrief.concept: Scope: the charter is your tool for holding the line kindly.
debrief.independent: Refer to the charter, make the fix an action item, and offer an in-scope alternative (move detail to a reading or the LMS).
debrief.escalateWhen: If scope creep persists, work with the practice area directors to find the cause; in the worst case escalate to the ODL director.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Change of Scope

events.title: Can We Add a Simulation?
events.text: {faculty} saw a colleague's custom interactive simulation. "Can we build one for Module 5? It would be perfect." It isn't in the charter.

choices.label: Ask what {fsub} wants students to learn from it, then have {ld} propose a way to meet that goal directly in Canvas.
choices.outcome: {ld} designs a scenario-based activity in Canvas. {faculty} likes it, and nothing new goes into scope.
choices.why: The SOP suggests discussing ways to reach the goal directly on the LMS when an interactive isn't in scope.

choices.label: Say yes. It'll make the course stand out.
choices.outcome: {faculty} is thrilled. {gd} is now building a custom interactive on top of every planned animation.
choices.why: Out-of-scope work with no trade-off lands on the team and the schedule.

choices.label: Tell {fobj} it's out of scope.
choices.outcome: Correct, but {fsub} feels shut down.
choices.why: Scope holds, but without an alternative it costs trust.

choices.label: Log it as a possible future project after launch.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} agrees to revisit after launch.
choices.why: Good scope control; even better is meeting the learning goal now within scope.

choices.label: Ask {sup} whether ODL can take on the extra work.
choices.outcome: {sup} asks whether you explored an in-scope option first.
choices.why: Explore in-scope options before asking for more resources.

debrief.concept: Scope: go back to the learning goal behind the request.
debrief.independent: Ask what the request is for. Propose an in-scope way to reach the same goal, often directly in the LMS.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate when the faculty member insists on out-of-scope work after you've offered alternatives.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Change of Scope

events.title: Somebody Else Booked the Studio
events.text: {mp}: "The studio and two of our crew are booked for another project on our shoot days. Our dates were never blocked on the media calendar."

choices.label: Book the next open dates and block every remaining production day on the media calendar now. Have {ld} build the master site with video placeholders meanwhile.
choices.outcome: You lose a week of shooting, but the build keeps moving and it won't happen again.
choices.why: Blocking production days is a PM duty in the SOP; re-sequencing keeps the rest of the team productive.

choices.label: Book the next open dates.
choices.outcome: New dates are set. The other remaining days are still unblocked.
choices.why: Fixes today's problem but not the cause.

choices.label: Ask {mp} to shoot on a Saturday.
choices.outcome: The shoot happens, with a tired crew.
choices.why: Overtime as a first resort costs morale and quality.

choices.label: Ask {sup} and the directors whether the other project can swap a day, with the impact on our launch.
choices.outcome: The other project swaps one day. You still need to block the rest.
choices.why: Reasonable for a shared-resource conflict, but the root cause, blocking calendars, is yours to fix.

choices.label: Wait for the studio to free up.
choices.outcome: Three weeks pass before the cameras roll.
choices.why: Production sits on the critical path; waiting moves the launch.

debrief.concept: Protect the critical path: production dates are scarce.
debrief.independent: As soon as production dates are known, block them on the media team's calendar. When a path stalls, re-sequence other work (placeholders in the master site).
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate for shared-resource conflicts you can't resolve with the other project's PM.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Design phase (block media calendars); LD SOP: placeholders

events.title: Two Videos Will Be a Week Late
events.text: {mp}: "Modules 7 and 8 will be a week late. The audio from the shoot needs more cleanup than I planned."

choices.label: Meet with {mp} and {ld}, check that {ld} still has time to place the videos before launch, have {ld} finish the rest of the site first, then get a clear change approval and update Asana.
choices.outcome: {ld} reorders the build. The late videos slot in with days to spare.
choices.why: This is the SOP's worked example: surface knock-on effects, let design prioritize the rest of the LMS, document the change.

choices.label: Update the dates in Asana.
choices.outcome: {ld} notices the new dates a week later.
choices.why: Silent date changes skip the conversation about knock-on effects.

choices.label: Ask {mp} to hit the original date anyway.
choices.outcome: The videos arrive on time with audio issues QA will find.
choices.why: Pressure shifts the problem into quality.

choices.label: Ask the directors whether another producer can take some editing.
choices.outcome: A second editor helps for two weeks.
choices.why: A valid SOP option when internal changes can't be accommodated; here a re-sequence would have been enough.

debrief.concept: Knock-on effects: every slip lands on someone downstream.
debrief.independent: Meet with the affected team, review the timeline, surface knock-on effects, and make them manageable (re-order the build). Get clear approval, then update Asana.
debrief.escalateWhen: When the change can't be absorbed internally, work with the directors on shifting work between team members or revising scope.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: When Things Go Wrong, With Timelines

events.title: Forty Notes on Rough Cut 2
events.text: {faculty} sent 40 notes on Rough Cut 2. About half are fixes; the other half rewrite content {fsub} approved in the script.

choices.label: Meet with {faculty} and {mp} to sort fixes from new content. Schedule one more rough cut for fixes; move new content to a reading or after launch.
choices.outcome: A third rough cut handles the fixes. The new material becomes a short reading.
choices.why: The media SOP allows extra rough cuts when notes keep coming; the charter and approved scripts define what counts as a fix.

choices.label: Apply all 40 notes.
choices.outcome: {mp} starts re-editing whole sections.
choices.why: Treating new content as fixes is scope creep at the most expensive stage.

choices.label: Email {fobj} that only fixes will be applied.
choices.outcome: Right call, rough delivery. {Fsub} feels dismissed.
choices.why: The decision is right; a conversation with an alternative would have kept trust.

choices.label: Send the notes to {sup} to decide.
choices.outcome: {sup} asks you to sort them first.
choices.why: Sorting notes is PM and producer work.

debrief.concept: Review windows: separate fixes from changes.
debrief.independent: Sort feedback into fixes and new requests, use extra rough cuts for fixes, and redirect new content using the charter.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if late-stage changes keep threatening the delivery date.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 4M Post-Production; PM SOP: Change of Scope

events.title: "Nobody Told Me Scripts Were Due"
events.text: {faculty}: "I didn't know scripts were due this week." The deadline was in three meeting summary emails.

choices.label: Learn how {fsub} reads email. Move key asks and dates to the top of the Friday weekly summary, and share a one-page development timeline.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} reads Friday summaries. Deadlines stop being surprises.
choices.why: The SOP: find out which emails a faculty member reads, put careful thought into the weekly summary, and use a development timeline to track progress.

choices.label: Forward the three emails that mentioned the deadline.
choices.outcome: Technically right. Relationship worse.
choices.why: Proving you sent it doesn't fix how {fsub} receives information.

choices.label: Send a reminder email before every deadline from now on.
choices.outcome: More emails, some of which {fsub} reads.
choices.why: Adding email volume works against busy faculty.

choices.label: Copy {fpos} department chair on future reminders.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} feels policed.
choices.why: Going around a partner damages trust and isn't how ODL escalates.

debrief.concept: Communication: match the channel to how the person actually reads.
debrief.independent: Ask which messages they read; use meeting summaries and Friday weekly summaries deliberately, lead with asks and dates, and share a visible development timeline.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue unless deadlines keep slipping after you've adapted.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Summary emails; Challenging Faculty

events.title: {ld} Is Stretched Thin
events.text: {ld} mentions being lead designer on four other courses. {ld}'s milestone check-ins have gotten shorter, and the master site is behind.

choices.label: Hold a 1:1, agree what this course needs from {ld} each week, and simplify the module template to cut non-essential build work.
choices.outcome: {ld} is relieved. A simpler template saves hours.
choices.why: Early, direct conversations and small scope trims protect both quality and morale.

choices.label: Bring {sup} {ld}'s workload and ask whether a supporting designer can help for a month.
choices.outcome: A supporting designer takes two modules.
choices.why: Good: cross-project workload is a leadership decision. Talking to {ld} first would have been better.

choices.label: Remind {ld} of the deadline and ask for a push.
choices.outcome: {ld} works late. Mistakes pile up quietly.
choices.why: Overload shows up as errors before it shows up as missed dates.

choices.label: Offer to build some Canvas pages yourself.
choices.outcome: Kind, but {ld} now has to check your pages against the design.
choices.why: Doing team members' work pulls the PM off coordination and often adds rework.

debrief.concept: Team health: overload causes errors first and delays second.
debrief.independent: Talk early, agree priorities, and trim polish that doesn't serve learning.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate when overload comes from other projects; shifting work across people is decided with the directors.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: With Timelines (shifting work between team members)

events.title: No Captions Ordered
events.text: {ld}: "The first videos are in Panopto, but no captions were ordered. I can't embed them until they're accessible."

choices.label: Have {mp} order and QA captions now, and add the distribution checklist (upload, captions, thumbnails, embed codes) to every video's task in Asana.
choices.outcome: Captions arrive in days, and the checklist catches the remaining videos.
choices.why: Captions ordered and QA'd are part of the media SOP's distribution step; making the checklist visible prevents repeats.

choices.label: Use Panopto's automatic captions without review.
choices.outcome: Fast, but technical terms come out garbled.
choices.why: Captions must be QA'd, not just generated.

choices.label: Launch without captions and add them later.
choices.outcome: QA will flag every video.
choices.why: Accessibility is a launch requirement.

choices.label: Ask {ld} to post transcripts instead.
choices.outcome: {ld} loses a day doing media work.
choices.why: Transcripts are part of distribution, which belongs to media.

debrief.concept: Quality is planned in: use the checklist, every time.
debrief.independent: Hold media to the distribution checklist for every asset, and track it where the team works.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if captioning services or budget are unavailable.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 7M Distribution

events.title: Where Are the Embed Codes?
events.text: {ld} has been hunting through Slack and Panopto for an hour: the embed codes and in-video quiz timestamps were never shared.

choices.label: Ask {mp} to document every embed code and quiz timestamp in the shared learning asset list, and make that the handoff point from now on.
choices.outcome: One list, one place. {ld} embeds the rest in an afternoon.
choices.why: The media SOP has producers document embed codes and share them with the designer; the LD SOP's asset list is the natural home.

choices.label: Let {ld} keep looking; the codes will turn up.
choices.outcome: {ld} finds most of them.
choices.why: Handoffs that depend on hunting cost the downstream person time.

choices.label: Ask {mp} to Slack {ld} the codes.
choices.outcome: Solved for today; next batch, same problem.
choices.why: Fixes the instance, not the handoff.

debrief.concept: Handoffs: define where work passes from one team to another.
debrief.independent: Agree one shared place (the asset list) where media hands assets to design, and make it part of the checklist.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 7M Distribution; LD SOP: Milestone 3 asset list

events.title: The Guest Didn't Sign a Release
events.text: {faculty} brought a graduate student on camera for a demonstration. {mp} just realized there's no signed release form.

choices.label: Get the release signed before any cut is shared, name it to convention, file it in the project's Admin folder, and add releases to the production checklist.
choices.outcome: Signed the next day. Nothing delayed.
choices.why: Release forms are a pre-production step in the media SOP, and the PM SOP names where they're stored.

choices.label: Use the footage; she's a student here.
choices.outcome: The footage goes in without permission.
choices.why: Using someone's likeness without a release is a real risk to the university.

choices.label: Cut the demonstration.
choices.outcome: Safe, but the module loses its best moment.
choices.why: Getting the signature would have kept it.

choices.label: Ask {sup} how to handle it.
choices.outcome: {sup} says: get it signed.
choices.why: The process is documented; you can follow it.

debrief.concept: Risk: paperwork before publishing.
debrief.independent: Collect releases before anyone appears on camera when possible, and always before footage is shared. File them by the naming convention.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if the person refuses to sign and the footage is essential.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 2M Release Forms; PM SOP: Google Drive structure

events.title: Who Owns These Videos?
events.text: {faculty} asks whether {fsub} can reuse the lecture videos after moving to another university. No IP agreement has been drafted.

choices.label: Draft the IP agreement from past examples and the university policy, and finalize it with the ODL director.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} gets a clear answer in writing within two weeks.
choices.why: Drafting IP agreements during development is a PM responsibility in the SOP, finalized with the director.

choices.label: Tell {fobj} the university owns everything.
choices.outcome: That's not necessarily what the policy says, and now {fsub}'s upset.
choices.why: Never answer legal-ish questions from memory.

choices.label: Tell {fobj} you'll ask the director.
choices.outcome: The director asks you to draft it.
choices.why: The director finalizes, but the PM drafts.

choices.label: Say you'll sort it out after launch.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} hesitates to approve the final cuts.
choices.why: Unresolved rights questions stall approvals.

debrief.concept: Agreements protect everyone: get rights in writing during development.
debrief.independent: Draft from the template and past examples, check the university IP policy, and review with the ODL director.
debrief.escalateWhen: The director finalizes the agreement; you bring the draft.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Development (IP agreements)

events.title: Copyright Snag
events.text: A textbook chapter and two figures {faculty} relies on can't be posted in the online course as files.

choices.label: Ask the library about library reserves or linking, have {ld} add a placeholder, and bring {faculty} open alternatives for the figures.
choices.outcome: Library reserves cover the chapter; open figures replace the rest.
choices.why: Go to the specialists, and bring the faculty member choices. The LD SOP already plans placeholders for library reserves.

choices.label: Post them anyway; only enrolled students can see them.
choices.outcome: It goes in. QA will flag it.
choices.why: Restricted access doesn't make posting legal.

choices.label: Drop the chapter and figures.
choices.outcome: Clean, but {faculty} has to rework the module.
choices.why: Removing content without alternatives hurts the course.

choices.label: Ask {sup} what to do.
choices.outcome: {sup} points you to the library.
choices.why: Know your campus experts and go to them directly.

debrief.concept: Risk: know your campus experts and bring alternatives.
debrief.independent: Go to the people who own the question (library, copyright), and offer the faculty member options rather than a problem.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if the faculty member refuses compliant alternatives.
debrief.sop: LD SOP: Development (placeholders for library reserves)

events.title: Set Up the Publisher Homework Tool
events.text: {faculty} wants {ld} to configure the textbook publisher's homework tool in the master site this week.

choices.label: Add a placeholder in the master site, and document in the hand-off guide that the instructor of record activates and configures it on the live site.
choices.outcome: Layout complete; setup steps are written for {fpos} term.
choices.why: The LD SOP: external tools get placeholders and are configured by the instructor of record on the live site.

choices.label: Have {ld} configure it now.
choices.outcome: It's set up in the master site, then breaks when migrated.
choices.why: Tool configuration belongs on the live site, by the instructor of record.

choices.label: Tell {fobj} that's {fpos} job.
choices.outcome: True, unhelpfully put.
choices.why: Explain the process and support {fobj} with hand-off documentation.

debrief.concept: Know the boundaries: what ODL builds and what the instructor owns.
debrief.independent: Use placeholders and clear hand-off documentation for tools the instructor configures.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue.
debrief.sop: LD SOP: Master Site Completion

events.title: Launch Is Close and No Hand-off Is Scheduled
events.text: {sup} asks: "When's the hand-off meeting with {faculty}? Is the hand-off document started?" Neither is.

choices.label: Schedule the hand-off meeting now, and start the hand-off document with {ld} (deliverables, maintenance instructions, resources), with the design document and links to every deliverable.
choices.outcome: {faculty} blocks the time. The document is ready before the meeting.
choices.why: The PM SOP's delivery checklist: hand-off document with the lead designer, all deliverables compiled, PM runs the meeting.

choices.label: Email {faculty} the course link on launch day.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} has a course but no idea how to maintain it.
choices.why: A link isn't a hand-off.

choices.label: Ask {ld} to handle the hand-off.
choices.outcome: {ld} does it on top of QA.
choices.why: The designer drafts with you, but the PM owns the hand-off meeting.

debrief.concept: Delivery: finish the project, not just the course.
debrief.independent: Plan the hand-off weeks ahead: document, deliverables, meeting, follow-ups. Then run the retrospective.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Delivery; Retrospective

events.title: QA Turns Up a Pile of Issues
events.text: {ld}'s first QA pass on the live course found broken links, two quizzes with wrong settings, and a module unpublished. Launch is days away.

choices.label: Triage with {ld}: fix launch-blocking issues first (settings, publishing, links in Module 1), log the rest with owners, and re-run the QA checklist before launch.
choices.outcome: Blockers are fixed in a day; the rest are scheduled and tracked.
choices.why: The LD SOP's QA step covers content, technology and platform with a checklist; triage protects launch day.

choices.label: Ask {ld} to fix everything before doing anything else.
choices.outcome: Everything gets fixed, slowly, with the critical items mixed in with cosmetic ones.
choices.why: Fixing all of it is fine, but without priorities the launch-blocking issues wait in line.

choices.label: Launch as is and patch during week one.
choices.outcome: Students find the broken quiz first.
choices.why: Known issues at launch hit students and the faculty member's first impression.

choices.label: Tell {sup} and ask whether launch should move.
choices.outcome: {sup} asks which issues actually block launch.
choices.why: Moving a term launch is rarely an option; triage first, then escalate if blockers remain.

debrief.concept: Launch readiness: separate blockers from polish.
debrief.independent: Run the QA checklist early, triage by impact on students, assign owners, and re-check before launch.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if launch-blocking issues can't be fixed before the course opens.
debrief.sop: LD SOP: Step 4 Implementation, QA checks

events.title: A New Module, Two Weeks Out
events.text: {faculty}: "I just got back from a conference. I want to add a module on a new study everyone's talking about. Just one short video and a reading?"

choices.label: Acknowledge the idea, point to the charter's eight modules, and offer to add it as an announcement and reading now with a full module considered for next term.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} posts it as a discussion prompt and adds the module to {fpos} wish list.
choices.why: Hold scope with the charter and offer an in-scope way to include the idea now.

choices.label: Say yes; it's just one video.
choices.outcome: {mp} books an extra shoot two weeks before launch.
choices.why: A small yes late in development costs the most.

choices.label: Agree to add a reading only.
choices.outcome: A reading gets added; {fsub}'s mostly satisfied.
choices.why: A good compromise, but it still changes scope without referencing the charter or the team.

choices.label: Tell {fobj} you'll check with {sup}.
choices.outcome: {sup} points back to the charter.
choices.why: You have the charter; use it first.

debrief.concept: Late changes cost the most; the charter is your anchor.
debrief.independent: Thank them, reference the agreed scope, and offer an in-scope option now plus a path for later.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if the faculty member insists and the change threatens launch.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Change of Scope; Drafting a Charter

events.title: Animate Before Scripts Are Final?
events.text: {gd}: "{mp} asked me to start the animations now to save time, but the scripts aren't final. If the narration changes, I redo the timing."

choices.label: Have {gd} create design frames for sign-off now, and start animating each segment once its script is final.
choices.outcome: Style is approved early, and animation starts on locked scripts.
choices.why: The media SOP confirms art style with design frames before animating; locking scripts first prevents rework.

choices.label: Start animating now; changes will be small.
choices.outcome: Two segments are re-timed when narration changes.
choices.why: Animating against draft scripts builds in rework.

choices.label: Have {gd} wait until all scripts are final.
choices.outcome: {gd} waits two weeks with little to do.
choices.why: Safe, but design frames and branding could have used the time.

choices.label: Ask {sup} to decide.
choices.outcome: {sup} asks what you'd recommend.
choices.why: This is a sequencing call you can make with the team.

debrief.concept: Sequencing: start the work that won't change.
debrief.independent: Do the stable work first (design frames, branding, templates) and start dependent work when its inputs are locked.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue unless the schedule truly can't wait for final scripts.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 2M Design Frame, 5M Animations

events.title: The Director Rejects the Animation Style
events.text: The media director saw {gd}'s rough animations and wants a different visual style. Nobody had signed off on the design frames.

choices.label: Meet with {gd}, {mp} and the director: agree the style on one design frame, reuse what fits, re-plan the remaining segments and their knock-on effects, and add director sign-off to the checklist.
choices.outcome: One afternoon settles the style; most assets carry over.
choices.why: Get the right sign-off at the design-frame stage, and when it's missed, re-plan visibly with the people affected.

choices.label: Ask {gd} to redo everything in the new style.
choices.outcome: {gd} starts over, quietly discouraged.
choices.why: Redoing everything ignores what can be reused and the schedule impact.

choices.label: Tell the director it's too late to change.
choices.outcome: The director approves nothing until the style changes.
choices.why: The director signs off on media; you need that sign-off.

choices.label: Bring {sup} the impact on launch and a proposed compromise style.
choices.outcome: {sup} helps broker the compromise.
choices.why: Reasonable, but the team can meet the director directly first.

debrief.concept: Approvals belong early: get sign-off where change is cheap.
debrief.independent: Build sign-off points into the plan (design frames, rough cuts). When one is missed, meet, salvage and re-plan openly.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if the style change would move the launch date.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 1M Director sign-off, 2M Design Frame

events.title: A Typo on Every Lower Third
events.text: {faculty} spotted that {fpos} title is wrong on the lower thirds in every final cut.

choices.label: Have {gd} fix the template once, {mp} re-export affected videos, and add a name-and-title check to the final-cut last looks.
choices.outcome: Fixed everywhere in a day, and the checklist catches the next one.
choices.why: Fix at the source, then add the check that would have caught it.

choices.label: Fix the video {faculty} mentioned.
choices.outcome: The other videos still have the typo.
choices.why: Fixing one instance leaves the rest.

choices.label: It's minor; leave it.
choices.outcome: {faculty} feels it's careless.
choices.why: Names and titles matter to faculty and students.

debrief.concept: Quality: fix the template, not just the instance.
debrief.independent: Correct the shared asset, re-check every place it's used, and add the missing check to the review step.
debrief.escalateWhen: Not an escalation issue.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 4M Final Cut last looks, 6M Lower Thirds

events.title: Where Did These Images Come From?
events.text: The Canvas banners look great, but {gd} isn't sure two of the stock images are licensed for university use.

choices.label: Check the licenses; replace anything unclear with licensed or university-provided images, and record sources in the asset list.
choices.outcome: Two images are swapped; every source is documented.
choices.why: Unclear rights are a risk; documenting sources makes the hand-off clean.

choices.label: Keep them; nobody checks banners.
choices.outcome: QA flags them right before launch.
choices.why: Unlicensed images are a real risk to the university.

choices.label: Ask {sup} whether the images are OK.
choices.outcome: {sup} suggests checking the licenses.
choices.why: You can verify this yourselves.

debrief.concept: Rights and licensing apply to every asset, not just readings.
debrief.independent: Verify licenses, replace what's unclear, and keep sources in the asset list.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if a required asset can't be licensed.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 6M Branding; LD SOP: Milestone 3 asset list

events.title: Two Producers, One Designer
events.text: {gd} is getting requests directly from {mp} and from a producer on another project, each saying theirs is urgent.

choices.label: Route graphics requests for your project through Asana with dates, agree priorities with {gd}, and talk to the other project's PM about overlap.
choices.outcome: {gd} has one list and clear priorities.
choices.why: A single, visible intake makes priorities explicit and protects focus.

choices.label: Tell {gd} your project comes first.
choices.outcome: The other producer escalates.
choices.why: Claiming priority without coordinating just moves the conflict.

choices.label: Ask {sup} to set priorities across the two projects, with both deadlines laid out.
choices.outcome: {sup} sets an order; it takes a few days.
choices.why: Cross-project priorities are a leadership call, but organizing your own intake comes first.

choices.label: Let {gd} sort it out.
choices.outcome: {gd} juggles both and rushes.
choices.why: Leaving a shared resource to absorb conflicting asks causes errors.

debrief.concept: Shared people need one queue and clear priorities.
debrief.independent: Make requests visible in one place with dates, and coordinate with other PMs who share the person.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate when two projects' priorities genuinely conflict and the PMs can't agree.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: With Timelines (shifting work between team members)

events.title: The Asana Board Is Fiction
events.text: Your first week on the rescue project: the Asana board shows tasks done that aren't, and dates from a plan nobody follows. {ld}: "Honestly, we stopped looking at it."

choices.label: Hold a timeline reset with {ld}, {mp} and {gd}: rebuild the board from real status working back from launch, get the revised timeline approved by the directors, then send {faculty} a clear summary.
choices.outcome: Everyone sees the same, real plan for the first time in weeks.
choices.why: The PM SOP: work backwards from delivery, align design and media timelines, and get director review before changes go into Asana.

choices.label: Quietly update the dates in Asana yourself.
choices.outcome: The board looks better; the team still doesn't trust it.
choices.why: A board nobody helped build won't be used.

choices.label: Skip Asana and track it in your head.
choices.outcome: Nobody knows what's due.
choices.why: A shared, current plan is the PM's main tool.

choices.label: Tell {sup} the board is a mess.
choices.outcome: {sup} agrees and asks for your reset plan.
choices.why: Bring the plan, not just the problem.

debrief.concept: Taking over a project: re-baseline before you manage it.
debrief.independent: Find out real status from the people doing the work, rebuild the timeline backwards from launch, and get it approved.
debrief.escalateWhen: Revised timelines need director review; bring the analysis.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Design phase (timeline), Building an Asana board

events.title: "The Last PM Promised Me..."
events.text: {faculty}: "Your predecessor promised me twelve videos and a custom case-study tool. I want to know that still happens." The charter lists eight videos.

choices.label: Meet 1:1 to listen, acknowledge the frustration, walk through the charter together, and offer an in-scope plan for the case studies in Canvas.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} is still cautious, but feels heard and agrees to the charter.
choices.why: Rebuild trust first, then anchor scope in the signed charter with an alternative.

choices.label: Honor the promises to rebuild trust.
choices.outcome: {faculty} is happy; the team is now far behind.
choices.why: Undocumented promises aren't scope; agreeing adds work you can't deliver.

choices.label: Email {fobj} the charter and say that's the scope.
choices.outcome: Correct, and it lands badly.
choices.why: Right scope, wrong delivery for a frustrated partner.

choices.label: Bring {sup} the promise gap and propose a joint meeting to reset scope.
choices.outcome: {sup} joins; scope is reset to the charter.
choices.why: Good when the gap is large, but a 1:1 first shows ownership.

debrief.concept: Inherited relationships: listen, then reset against the charter.
debrief.independent: Start with a 1:1 to understand what was promised, then anchor to the charter and offer in-scope alternatives.
debrief.escalateWhen: Bring in ODL leadership if the faculty member won't accept the charter scope.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Challenging Faculty; Change of Scope; Drafting a Charter

events.title: The Location Needs a Permit
events.text: {mp}: "The lab we're filming in needs a facilities permit, and we'll have bystanders in the background. Shoot is in three weeks."

choices.label: Have {mp} file the permit today, prepare release forms for anyone on camera, and you handle booking and blocking the shoot dates on the media calendar.
choices.outcome: Permit approved, releases signed on the day.
choices.why: The media SOP lists scouting, permits and release forms in pre-production; the PM supports booking and calendars.

choices.label: Film without the permit; it's on campus.
choices.outcome: Facilities stops the shoot halfway.
choices.why: Skipping permits risks the shoot and the relationship with the location.

choices.label: Move the shoot to the studio instead.
choices.outcome: Easier, but {faculty} loses the documentary look {fsub} wanted.
choices.why: Changes the creative direction the charter agreed to.

choices.label: Ask {sup} to sort out the permit.
choices.outcome: {sup} points you to facilities.
choices.why: This is routine pre-production.

debrief.concept: Pre-production protects production days.
debrief.independent: Work the logistics checklist early: scouting, permits, release forms, booking, calendars.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if a permit is denied and the location is essential.
debrief.sop: Media SOP: 2M Scouting, Booking/Permits/Travel, Release Forms

events.title: {faculty} Will Be Abroad on Shoot Day
events.text: {faculty} just accepted a keynote overseas. It overlaps the shoot dates, which were never put on {fpos} calendar.

choices.label: Find new dates with {faculty}, {mp} and the crew in one meeting, block them on everyone's calendar, and move review windows so post-production isn't squeezed.
choices.outcome: New dates are locked on every calendar.
choices.why: The PM SOP: schedule with everyone present and block production days on calendars.

choices.label: Record {fpos} interview remotely from the hotel.
choices.outcome: The footage doesn't match the documentary look.
choices.why: Workable, but changes quality agreed in the brief.

choices.label: Ask {fobj} to skip the keynote.
choices.outcome: {Fsub} declines, annoyed.
choices.why: Faculty commitments come first; plan around them.

choices.label: Ask {sup} to approve moving the shoot, with the impact.
choices.outcome: Approved; you schedule it.
choices.why: Fine if milestones move, but you can schedule first.

debrief.concept: Calendars are commitments: block them early with everyone.
debrief.independent: Get production dates on the faculty member's and media team's calendars as soon as they're known.
debrief.escalateWhen: Escalate if a date change moves an approved milestone.
debrief.sop: PM SOP: Scheduling meetings; Design phase (block media calendars)
